newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish KPW approves first firm for OTC trade.
newsitem.headline: Polish KPW approves first firm for OTC trade.

text.p: The Polish Securities Commission (KPW) on Thursday approved the listing of shares in machine tool maker Rafamet SA for trade in the over-the- counter market, the first firm to receive approval.
"Rafamet is considered a publicly traded firm just like any other," KPW head Jacek Socha told reporters.
All Rafamet's 1,439,567 shares were approved for trade.
Czeslaw Gawlowski, president of the OTC market to be called Centralna Tabela Ofert (CeTO), said trade could begin by December 15.
"I hope this (Rafamet's OTC entry) will help firms that so far have been only thinking about entering the over-the- counter market to transform this thinking into concrete actions," he said.

Gawlowski told Reuters last month that many companies might prefer to enter CeTO rather than the Warsaw bourse's second or third floor because the requirements and costs were much lower, but there was similar access to capital.
He said many speculative investors might switch from the Warsaw bourse to the OTC market as the latter, much more risky, would offer more opportunities for fast, large profits.
Rafamet made a net profit of 9.6 million zlotys last year on sales of 30.8 millon zlotys and earned 76,200 zlotys over this year's first half on sales of 20.4 million zlotys.
Its main shareholders are Bank Handlowy SA and Bank Slaski, with 38.16 percent each, and the state treasury, with 23.68 percent.
